hypotheses.justification: `Measure.prod μ ν` is defined for arbitrary ν. By its definition in Prod.lean it is `if SFinite ν then bind μ (fun x => map (Prod.mk x) ν) else 0`. The statement therefore elaborates without `SFinite ν`. If ν is not s-finite, both `(c • μ).prod ν` and `μ.prod ν` are `0`, so the goal reads `0 = c • 0`, which holds because scalar multiplication preserves zero on `Measure`. If ν is s-finite, the existing proof applies unchanged. The proof is `by_cases h : SFinite ν`, with the existing proof in the positive case. In the negative case, unfold `Measure.prod`, rewrite with `h`, and close with `smul_zero`. The other variable `[SFinite μ]` is not an argument, because the theorem's own `{μ : Measure α}` binder shadows the variable μ. So `hν` is the only s-finite hypothesis the theorem takes, and it can be deleted.
